FS116-N1-GERM-R: in a valid k-coloured fragment on a closed disc of radius above 1 about a point p, for any k, Siamese pairs allowed, let y = r(ψ) be a point of ω(p), c a colour, and v⁻, v⁺, u⁻, u⁺ the arcs of ω(p) just clockwise and just counter-clockwise of r(ψ − 60°) and r(ψ + 60°); if v⁻ lies in the closure of a tile of colour c, no tile of colour c approaches y along a direction β with β − ψ in (150°, 330°); for v⁺ the interval is (−30°, 150°), for u⁻ (−150°, 30°), and for u⁺ (30°, 210°) *Not claimed:* anything about tiles that approach y only along the boundary directions ψ + 150°, ψ + 330°, ψ − 30°, ψ + 30°, ψ + 210°, ψ − 150°; anything when a germ lies on Γ with colour c on neither side
FS116-N1-GERM-S: in a valid fragment on a closed disc of radius above 1 about a vertex p of at least four colours, Siamese pairs allowed, let y be a change point of the ring, X the colour of the ring just counter-clockwise of y and X̄ the colour just clockwise, and u⁻, u⁺, v⁻, v⁺ the arcs of ω(p) just clockwise and just counter-clockwise of the ring points y + 60° and y − 60°; then p has four colours and no more, X and X̄ are the colours absent at p, and (i) if neither v⁻ nor u⁺ lies on a (Q) arc, every direction at y in the open cone of 60° about the direction to p lies in the cone of a tile of a colour c of p every tile of p of which colour lies in B̄(y, 1); (ii) if neither u⁻ nor v⁺ lies on a (Q) arc, every direction at y in the open cone of 60° about the direction away from p lies in the cone of a tile, not a tile of p, of a colour c of p every tile of p of which colour misses B(y, 1); (iii) if none of the four lies on a (Q) arc, y is a vertex of at least four colours *Not claimed:* anything at k ≥ 7; that the tile in (i) is a tile of p (that is RING-GERM, in the non-Siamese class); that a change point with a germ on a (Q) arc has fewer than four colours
FS116-N1-TOUCH: in a valid fragment on a closed disc of radius above 1 about a vertex p of four colours and no more, Siamese pairs allowed, let w be a point of ω(p) in the closure of a tile of one of p's colours which is not a change point of the ring and lies on no arc of Γ on ω(p), and suppose none of the four arcs of ω(p) just clockwise and just counter-clockwise of w + 60° and w − 60° lies on a (Q) arc; then the ring just clockwise and just counter-clockwise of w lies in tiles of one colour X absent at p, each of the four arcs lies in the closure of a tile of the other absent colour X̄ and of no tile of colour X, and no tile of colour X̄ has w in its closure *Not claimed:* that such a point exists in any fragment of SAT-QFREE's class; anything at k ≥ 7; anything when a germ lies on a (Q) arc
FS116-N1-ECHO: in a valid k-coloured fragment on a closed disc of radius above 2 about a point p, for any k, Siamese pairs allowed, let w be a point of ω(p) whose ring just clockwise and just counter-clockwise of w lies in tiles of one colour X absent at p; if the fragment is saturated at w and X is in w's essential multicolour, the point 2w − p lies in the closure of a tile of colour X *Not claimed:* anything when X has density 0 at w (a cusp); that the X-tile at 2w − p exists in any fragment of SAT-STRIP's class
FS116-N1-AXIS: let p be a degree-4 vertex of four colours of a valid fragment on a closed disc of radius above 1 about p, saturated on a disc about p, whose four edges are segments along the four half-axes, with tiles coloured c_I, c_II, c_III, c_IV by quadrant and absent colours X, X̄; then at q_N = p + (0, 1): (a) every tile approaching q_N along a direction below the horizontal has colour X or X̄; (b) a tile of colour c_IV approaches q_N along 0⁺ and one of colour c_III along 180⁻, both above the line y = 1; (c) the arcs of ω(p) just counter-clockwise of r(30°) and just clockwise of r(150°) lie on no (Q) arc; (d) if the arcs just clockwise of r(30°) and just counter-clockwise of r(150°) lie on no (Q) arc, every tile approaching q_N along a direction below the horizontal has one colour, and q_N is not a change point; and at each of the axis points q_E, q_W, q_S, read with the quadrants turned with it *Not claimed:* anything for four segments not at right angles; anything at k ≥ 7 for (d) (at k = 9 SQ9 fails it); that the axis points are touch points in any fragment saturated on B̄(p, 1); SAT-STRIP
